mainTopic: The end of רב מנשה's story with the thieves, the משנה and ברייתא on a Jewish woman delivering or nursing a נכרית's baby (and the reverse), and how far the concern of איבה reaches
overview: This amud finishes the story of רב מנשה. He tricks thieves by naming a far-off destination, and when they insult his teacher רב יהודה, he puts them under רב יהודה's ban. The ban works: the thieves fail for 22 years, and the one who will not have it lifted is eaten by a lion. A new משנה then teaches that a Jewish woman may not deliver or nurse a נכרית's baby. A נכרית may help a Jewish woman, but she may nurse only in the Jewish woman's domain. In a ברייתא, רבי מאיר forbids a נכרית midwife or nurse even when others are watching, because she could kill the baby secretly. The חכמים permit it when others are watching, and the גמרא explains why both cases had to be taught. רב יוסף then allows delivering a נכרית's baby for pay because of איבה (hostility). He tries to stretch this to delivering on שבת, to nursing, and to pulling someone out of a pit. Each time אביי answers that a believable excuse prevents איבה. The amud ends as רבי אבהו begins a related teaching before רבי יוחנן, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב מנשה outsmarts the thieves and curses them
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשה tells thieves he is going to far-away פומבדיתא, then leaves them at nearby בי תורתא. They call his teacher a swindler, so he puts them under the ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the way to בי תורתא, thieves met רב מנשה and asked where he was going. He said, 'To פומבדיתא.' When he reached בי תורתא, he left them. They said, 'You are a student of יהודה the swindler!' He answered, 'You know him? May it be God's will that these people be under his ban.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story that began earlier. רב מנשה uses a clever trick to protect himself from thieves, and when they insult his teacher he curses them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By naming a city farther away, רב מנשה made the thieves think they had plenty of time before striking. He then broke away early at the closer town. The thieves assumed he had learned this trick from his teacher רב יהודה, so they insulted him, and רב מנשה responded by placing them under רב יהודה's שמתא.

phrases.english: to Bei Torta.
Thieves encountered him.
They said to him: Where are you going?
He said to them: To Pumbedita.
phrases.notes: פומבדיתא was farther than בי תורתא, so the thieves thought they had more time before he left them.

phrases.english: When he arrived at Bei Torta, he separated from them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: תַּלְמִידָא דִּיהוּדָה רַמָּאָה אַתְּ!
phrases.english: They said to him: You are a student of Yehuda the swindler!
phrases.notes: They mean רב יהודה, his teacher.

phrases.english: He said to them: Do you know him?
May it be God's will that
these people be under his ban.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּגַעוּ בֵּיהּ גַּנָּבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a story begun on the previous page about how a Jew may protect himself on the road.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב מנשה used the trick of naming a farther destination and placed the insulting thieves under רב יהודה's ban.

steps.title: The ban takes effect on the thieves
steps.stepSummary: The thieves fail for 22 years and ask to have the ban lifted. One weaver refuses and is eaten by a lion, which matches a popular saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: They went and stole for twenty-two years, but they never succeeded. When they saw this, they all came and asked to have their ban removed. One weaver among them did not come to remove his ban, and a lion ate him. This is what people say: a weaver who is not humble loses a year from his life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב מנשה's curse really worked. It ends with a folk saying that fits the story of the stubborn weaver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban made all of their stealing fail for 22 years, until they humbled themselves and asked for it to be lifted. The weaver who stayed brazen was punished with death. The saying about a 'not shy' weaver losing years is shown to come true here.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban of a תלמיד חכם has real power. Those who humbled themselves were spared, and the stubborn one was punished.

phrases.english: They went and carried out thefts
for twenty-two years, but they were not successful.
Once they saw this, they all came
and asked about their ban.
phrases.notes: They were asking to have the ban taken off them.

phrases.english: But there was one weaver among them
who did not come to have his ban lifted.
A lion ate him.
This is what people say:
A weaver who is not humble,
a year is taken off his years.
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא has the words in round brackets. The corrected wording is in square brackets, and both mean the same thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַלוּ עֲבַדוּ גְּנֵיבָתָא עֶשְׂרִין וְתַרְתֵּין שְׁנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of the curse given in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban made the thieves fail. The weaver who refused to have it lifted died, which matches the popular saying.

steps.title: Thieves of בבל versus bandits of ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up the stories by pointing to the difference between the robbers of בבל and those of ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and see the difference between the thieves of בבל and the bandits of ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the set of road stories with a short comment comparing two kinds of robbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line looks back at both stories. In the earlier story, the bandits of ארץ ישראל reacted to רבי עקיבא's trick with respect. Here, the Babylonian thieves insulted רב יהודה when they saw the same kind of trick.
steps.whatToRemember: This ends the discussion of travelling with נכרים and robbers. The next line starts a brand-new משנה.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא חֲזִי, מָה בֵּין גַּנָּבֵי בָבֶל
phrases.english: Come and see the difference between the thieves of Babylonia
and the bandits of Eretz Yisrael.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא חֲזִי, מָה בֵּין גַּנָּבֵי בָבֶל וְלִסְטִין דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up this story together with the earlier story about the bandits of ארץ ישראל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The thieves of בבל were cruder than the bandits of ארץ ישראל. They insulted the חכם, while the bandits had praised him.

steps.title: משנה: delivering a baby
steps.stepSummary: A Jewish woman may not deliver a נכרית's baby, because that brings a child into the world for עבודה זרה. A נכרית may deliver a Jewish woman's baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Jewish woman may not act as a midwife for a non-Jewish woman, because she would be delivering a child who will serve idols. But a non-Jewish woman may deliver a Jewish woman's baby.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: a Jewish woman acting as a midwife for a non-Jewish woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given is that the Jewish midwife would be helping bring a child for עבודה זרה into the world. The reverse case is allowed. A נכרית may deliver a Jewish baby, so in this משנה the concern only goes one way.

keyTerms.meaning: Act as a midwife, deliver a baby

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תְּיַילֵּד אֶת הַנׇּכְרִית,
phrases.english: A Jewish woman may not deliver the baby of a gentile woman,
because she would be delivering a child for idol worship.
But a gentile woman may deliver the baby of a Jewish woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תְּיַילֵּד אֶת הַנׇּכְרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jewish woman may not deliver a נכרית's baby. A נכרית may deliver a Jewish baby.

steps.title: משנה: nursing a baby
steps.stepSummary: A Jewish woman may not nurse a נכרית's baby. A נכרית may nurse a Jewish baby, but only in the Jewish woman's domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Jewish woman may not nurse the child of a non-Jewish woman. But a non-Jewish woman may nurse the child of a Jewish woman, as long as she does it in the Jewish woman's domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה uses the same pattern for nursing as it did for delivering a baby, and adds one condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nursing a נכרית's baby would mean raising a child for עבודה זרה, the same reason given for delivering. In the reverse case, a נכרית may nurse a Jewish baby, but only בִּרְשׁוּתָהּ, in the Jewish woman's domain. This extra condition was not given for delivering.
steps.confusionAlert: בִּרְשׁוּתָהּ does not mean 'with her permission.' It means in the Jewish woman's domain.
steps.whatToRemember: Both rules follow one pattern: a Jewish woman may not help bring up a נכרית's child, but a נכרית may help a Jewish woman. For nursing, the נכרית must do it in the Jewish woman's domain.

phrases.aramaic: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תָּנִיק בְּנָהּ שֶׁל נׇכְרִית,
phrases.english: A Jewish woman may not nurse the child of a gentile woman,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נׇכְרִית מְנִיקָה בְּנָהּ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: but a gentile woman may nurse the child of a Jewish woman
in her domain.
phrases.notes: 'Her' means the Jewish woman. The nursing must happen in the Jewish woman's home.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תָּנִיק בְּנָהּ שֶׁל נׇכְרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same pattern to nursing and adds the condition of בִּרְשׁוּתָהּ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jewish woman may not nurse a נכרית's child. A נכרית may nurse a Jewish child, but only in the Jewish woman's domain.

steps.title: רבי מאיר forbids midwifery in both directions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a Jewish woman may not deliver a נכרית's baby because of עבודה זרה. A נכרית may not deliver a Jewish woman's baby because of fear of שפיכות דמים. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A Jewish woman may not deliver a non-Jewish woman's baby, because she would be bringing a child into the world who will serve idols. A non-Jewish woman may not deliver a Jewish woman's baby, because non-Jews are suspected of murder. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא on the topic of the משנה. In it, רבי מאיר forbids midwifery in both directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half matches the משנה: a Jewish woman should not help bring a child into the world for עבודה זרה. The second half is new and stricter. רבי מאיר does not let a נכרית deliver a Jewish baby at all, because he worries she will harm it.

keyTerms.meaning: Will act as a midwife, will deliver a baby

steps.confusionAlert: Step 4 (the משנה) said a נכרית MAY deliver a Jewish baby. That is not a contradiction. רבי מאיר here disagrees with that ruling, and the next step shows that the חכמים permit it with conditions.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תְּיַילֵּד אֶת הַנׇּכְרִית,
phrases.english: A Jewish woman may not deliver the baby of a non-Jewish woman,
because she is delivering a child for idol worship,

phrases.aramaic: וְנׇכְרִית לֹא תְּיַילֵּד אֶת בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: and a non-Jewish woman may not deliver the baby of a Jewish woman,
because they are suspected of bloodshed;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תְּיַילֵּד אֶת הַנׇּכְרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא with a stricter view than the משנה's ruling in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a נכרית may never serve as a midwife for a Jewish woman, because of the fear that she will kill the baby.

steps.title: The חכמים permit a נכרית midwife when others are watching
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים allow a נכרית to deliver a Jewish baby as long as other women stand over her, but not when she is alone with the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: A non-Jewish woman may deliver a Jewish woman's baby when other women are standing over her, but not when the two of them are alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the opposing view of the חכמים. They allow a נכרית midwife under supervision.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים share the worry about harm, but they think other women watching are enough to prevent it. The only forbidden case is when the נכרית is alone with the Jewish mother.

keyTerms.meaning: "And the Sages say." This introduces the majority view that disagrees.
Between her and her, meaning the two of them alone

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
A non-Jewish woman may deliver the baby of a Jewish woman
when other women are standing over her,
but not when they are alone together.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר's ban on a נכרית midwife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נכרית may deliver a Jewish baby under the watch of other women, but not alone.

steps.title: רבי מאיר says watching women are not enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that even with others watching it is forbidden, because a midwife could press on the baby's temple and kill it without anyone noticing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר says: Even when other women are standing over her, it is still not allowed. Sometimes she places her hand on the baby's temple and kills him, and no one sees it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר explains why the חכמים's condition does not satisfy him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is about whether supervision really works. רבי מאיר points to a kind of killing that is invisible: pressure on the temple during delivery. Watching women would not catch it, so supervision gives no real protection.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ אֲחֵרוֹת עוֹמְדוֹת עַל גַּבָּהּ נָמֵי לָא,
phrases.english: Even when other women are standing over her, also not,
because sometimes she places her hand on his temple
and kills him, and it is not seen.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ אֲחֵרוֹת עוֹמְדוֹת עַל גַּבָּהּ נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי מאיר answers the חכמים's condition of supervision.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Supervision does not help, because the killing can be done secretly.

steps.title: A story of a boasting midwife supports רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: One non-Jewish woman insulted another by calling her a midwife for Jewish women. The midwife answered that she had shed as much Jewish baby blood as the foam of a river.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a certain woman who said to her friend: "Midwife of Jewish women, daughter of a midwife of Jewish women!" The other answered: "May that woman suffer as many evils as the blood I draw from them, like the foam of a river."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that seems to show רבי מאיר's fear is real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The midwife openly claims she killed many Jewish babies during deliveries. This matches רבי מאיר's worry that a נכרית midwife can kill without being noticed.

phrases.english: Like that woman who said to her friend:
Midwife of Jewish women, daughter of a midwife of Jewish women!
phrases.notes: This was meant as an insult, as if serving Jews were shameful.

phrases.english: She said to her:
May the evils of that woman be many,
phrases.notes: "That woman" really means the insulter herself. It is a curse aimed back at her.

phrases.english: as I draw out blood from them
like the foam of a river.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דַּאֲמַרָה לַחֲבֶרְתַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example backing רבי מאיר's worry.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's claim that a נכרית midwife may secretly kill Jewish babies.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story in which a non-Jewish midwife boasts of having killed many Jewish infants.

steps.title: The חכמים say she was only bragging
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the proof: the midwife was just boasting to look strong, not describing what she really did.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים would say to you: That is not so. She was only building herself up with words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the חכמים would answer the story that supported רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not deny the story happened. They deny that it proves anything. Her words were empty boasting to answer an insult, so the story gives no evidence that midwives really kill babies, and their ruling stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: She set herself up, built herself up

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר forbids a נכרית midwife even with others watching, because killing can be hidden. The חכמים permit it when others are watching. They treat the boasting midwife's story as empty talk.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis would say to you: It is not so,
it was merely with words that she was building herself up.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן אֲמַרוּ לָךְ: לָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the story as proof for רבי מאיר. It does not deny that the event happened.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The midwife's claim was empty boasting made in reply to an insult, not a true report of killings.

steps.title: רבי מאיר forbids nursing in both directions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about nursing. It brings a ברייתא where רבי מאיר forbids a Jewish woman to nurse a נכרית's child, and a נכרית to nurse a Jewish child.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a Jewish woman may not nurse. A ברייתא teaches: a Jewish woman may not nurse a non-Jewish woman's son, because she would be raising a child for עבודה זרה. A non-Jewish woman may not nurse a Jewish woman's son, because she is suspected of שפיכות דמים. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the משנה's next rule, about nursing, and brings a ברייתא that gives the reasons. This matches the midwife ברייתא from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each direction has its own reason. A Jewish nurse would be helping raise a child for עבודה זרה. A non-Jewish nurse is suspected of harming the Jewish baby.

phrases.english: A Jewish woman may not nurse.
The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תָּנִיק בְּנָהּ שֶׁל נׇכְרִית,
phrases.english: A Jewish woman may not nurse the son of a non-Jewish woman,
because she would be raising a child for idol worship,

phrases.aramaic: וְנׇכְרִית לֹא תָּנִיק אֶת בְּנָהּ שֶׁל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: and a non-Jewish woman may not nurse the son of a Jewish woman,
because she is suspected of bloodshed,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תָּנִיק בְּנָהּ שֶׁל נׇכְרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the midwife rule to the parallel nursing rule of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, nursing is forbidden in both directions: because of עבודה זרה in one direction and fear of שפיכות דמים in the other.

steps.title: The חכמים allow nursing when others are present
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים allow a נכרית to nurse a Jewish baby when other women stand over her, but not when she is alone with the baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: a non-Jewish woman may nurse a Jewish woman's son while other women stand over her, but not when she is alone with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give their opinion. They allow nursing when others are watching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים agree that there is a danger. But they think that people watching stops her from harming the baby. The only problem they see is being alone with him.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: נׇכְרִית מְנִיקָה אֶת בְּנָהּ שֶׁל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: A non-Jewish woman may nurse the son of a Jewish woman
when other women are standing over her,
but not when it is just him and her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: נׇכְרִית מְנִיקָה אֶת בְּנָהּ שֶׁל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נכרית may nurse a Jewish baby when others are present, but not when she is alone with him.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: poison on the breast cannot be seen
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that even people watching do not help. She could put poison on her breast beforehand and kill the baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: even when others stand over her it is not allowed, because sometimes she smears poison on her breast while outside, and it kills him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר explains why people watching is not enough in the nursing case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger here happens before anyone is watching. She can prepare the poison outside, and then the nursing itself harms the baby. So watching her nurse does not protect him.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ אֲחֵרוֹת עוֹמְדוֹת עַל גַּבָּהּ נָמֵי לָא,
phrases.english: even when others are standing over her, it is also not allowed,
because sometimes she smears poison for him
on her breast while outside, and kills him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ אֲחֵרוֹת עוֹמְדוֹת עַל גַּבָּהּ נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי מאיר answers the חכמים' condition about others watching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a נכרית may not nurse a Jewish baby even when others are present.

steps.title: Why the midwife case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the argument had to be taught for both cases. If we only had the midwife case, we might think the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר about nursing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary to teach both. If we had only learned the midwife case, we might say the חכמים permit it there because harming the baby is impossible with others watching. But with a nurse, who can smear poison on her breast while outside, we might say the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a צריכא. It is showing why the same argument appears twice, once for the midwife and once for the nurse. This is the first half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a midwife, everything happens in front of the women watching, so they can stop her. With a nurse, the poison is put on in secret beforehand. So from the midwife case alone, we could not know that the חכמים are lenient about nursing too.

keyTerms.meaning: it is necessary (to teach both cases)

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
for if it had taught us only the midwife,
it is in that case that the Rabbis say it is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר מִשּׁוּם דַּאֲחֵרוֹת רוֹאוֹת אוֹתָהּ,
phrases.english: since it is not possible, because others see her,
but a nurse,
where it is possible that she smears poison for him
on her breast while outside and kills him,
I might say they agree with Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּצְרִיכָא, דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן מְיַלֶּדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the מחלוקת had to be stated again after the midwife case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The midwife case alone would not show that the חכמים are lenient about nursing.

steps.title: Why the nursing case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the nursing case, we might think רבי מאיר agrees with the חכמים about a midwife. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we had only learned the nurse case, we might say רבי מאיר forbids it there because of poison smeared beforehand. But with a midwife, where harm is impossible with others standing over her, we might say he agrees with the חכמים. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכא with the opposite direction. Then it concludes that both cases are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nursing case shows how strict רבי מאיר is. But it would not show that he forbids even a supervised midwife. Each case teaches something the other cannot teach.
steps.whatToRemember: The midwife case teaches how strict רבי מאיר is (he forbids it even with others watching). The nursing case teaches how lenient the חכמים are (they permit it even though poison is possible).
steps.confusionAlert: This is only a 'might have thought.' In step 8, רבי מאיר already said a midwife could press on the baby's temple without anyone noticing, so he really does forbid the midwife case too.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only the nurse,
it is in that case that Rabbi Meir says it is forbidden,
because she smears poison for him
on her breast while outside and kills him,
but a midwife,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר הֵיכָא דַּאֲחֵרוֹת עוֹמְדוֹת עַל גַּבָּהּ,
phrases.english: where it is not possible when others are standing over her,
I might say he agrees with the Rabbis.
It is necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן מְנִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the צריכא, ending with the conclusion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both cases had to be taught. Each one shows a different side of the מחלוקת.

steps.title: A ברייתא allows delivering a non-Jewish baby for pay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a contradiction. A ברייתא says a Jewish woman may deliver an Aramean woman's baby for pay. But step 6 forbade it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: a Jewish woman may deliver an Aramean woman's baby for payment, but not for free!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from step 6 with a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 forbade a Jewish woman to deliver a נכרית's baby because of עבודה זרה. This ברייתא allows it, at least when she is paid. So the two sources seem to clash.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
A Jewish woman may deliver the baby of an Aramean woman for payment,
but not for free!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ: יְהוּדִית מְיַלֶּדֶת אֲרַמִּית בְּשָׂכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the midwife rule of the משנה (step 4), repeated in step 6, and challenges it with a different ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling, agreed on by everyone, that a Jewish woman may not deliver a נכרית's baby. It is stated in the משנה (step 4) and repeated in the ברייתא (step 6).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different ברייתא permits it for pay, which contradicts a total ban.

steps.title: רב יוסף: pay makes it permitted because of hostility
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that when she is paid it is permitted, to avoid creating איבה (hostility).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: for payment it is permitted, because of hostility.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף settles the contradiction. The basic ban stays in place, but there is an exception when she is paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is still that she should not deliver the baby. But turning down money for this would create anger against Jews. So for pay it is allowed. For free there is no such concern, so it stays forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that worry about איבה can change a rule in practice, even though the basic prohibition still stands.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
For payment it is permitted, because of hostility.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: בְּשָׂכָר שְׁרֵי מִשּׁוּם אֵיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception based on an outside concern (איבה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that delivering a נכרית's baby is basically allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is basically forbidden. When she is paid, it is permitted only to avoid איבה.

steps.title: רב יוסף wants to permit delivering on שבת for pay
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף suggests that a Jewish midwife may deliver a non-Jewish woman's baby on שבת if she is paid, because of איבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף wanted to say: delivering a non-Jewish woman's baby on שבת for pay is allowed, because of hostility.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף takes his איבה reasoning from step 17 and tries to push it further, even to breaking שבת. This sets up אביי's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17, איבה allowed paid delivery on a weekday. Now רב יוסף suggests it is strong enough to allow חילול שבת too. The words סבר למימר signal that this is only an idea he 'thought to say', and that it will soon be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say. This is a suggestion that usually gets rejected.
Hostility or ill-will that a refusal might cause

steps.confusionAlert: סבר רב יוסף למימר does not mean this is the הלכה. It is a suggestion that אביי is about to knock down.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef thought to say:
Delivering a gentile woman's baby on Shabbat
for pay is permitted, because of hostility.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר רַב יוֹסֵף לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב יוסף's איבה reasoning from a weekday delivery to a שבת delivery.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggested: paid delivery for a non-Jew is allowed even on שבת because of איבה.

steps.title: אביי: she has an easy excuse about שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the idea. The midwife can explain that Jews break שבת only for women who keep שבת, so no hostility will come from refusing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: she can tell the non-Jewish woman, 'For our women, who keep שבת, we break שבת. For yours, who don't keep שבת, we don't.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's suggestion. He shows that the midwife can refuse without causing hostility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איבה only matters when a refusal would look like plain hatred. Here the midwife has a reasonable explanation tied to keeping שבת, so the refusal won't be taken personally. Without איבה, the reason to permit חילול שבת falls away.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
She can say to her:
phrases.notes: 'She' is the Jewish midwife, and 'her' is the non-Jewish woman giving birth.

phrases.english: Ours, who keep Shabbat,
we desecrate Shabbat for them;
yours, who do not keep Shabbat,
we do not desecrate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: יָכְלָה לְמֵימַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's suggestion in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects stretching איבה to permit חילול שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no real איבה, because the midwife has a believable, non-hateful excuse.

steps.title: רב יוסף wants to permit paid nursing
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף suggests that a Jewish woman may nurse a non-Jewish baby for pay, because of איבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף wanted to say: nursing a non-Jewish baby for pay is allowed, because of hostility.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tries the same איבה reasoning on the nursing case from the earlier steps. This sets up another reply from אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nursing a non-Jewish baby was forbidden earlier in the סוגיא. רב יוסף suggests that payment, together with the fear of איבה, should change the ruling, just as it did for the midwife.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef thought to say:
Nursing for pay is permitted because of hostility.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר רַב יוֹסֵף לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same איבה reasoning to a second case, nursing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggested: paid nursing of a non-Jewish baby is allowed because of איבה.

steps.title: אביי: she has an excuse whether single or married
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the idea. A single woman can say she wants to get married, and a married woman can say she doesn't want to become unattractive to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: she can make an excuse. If she is single, 'I want to get married.' If she is married, 'I don't want to make myself repulsive to my husband.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי again shows that the Jewish woman can refuse politely, so there is no איבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי covers both possibilities, a single woman and a married woman, so every Jewish woman has a ready excuse. Because the refusal sounds personal and reasonable, it won't cause hostility, and the original איסור stays in place.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
She can say, if she is unmarried:
"I want to get married,"
if she is a married woman:
"I will not make myself repulsive to my husband."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: יָכְלָה לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's suggestion in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects permitting paid nursing because of איבה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Every woman, single or married, has a believable personal excuse, so no איבה results.

steps.title: רב יוסף wants to permit pulling a non-Jew out of a pit for pay
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא that says we don't raise or lower non-Jews and small-animal shepherds. He suggests that raising them for pay is allowed because of איבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף wanted to say about the ברייתא, 'Non-Jews and shepherds of small animals, we don't raise them up and we don't lower them down': raising them up for pay is allowed, because of hostility.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tries his איבה idea a third time, now on a ברייתא about helping someone out of a pit. This sets up אביי's final reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids pulling these people out of a pit. רב יוסף suggests that payment plus איבה permits at least the raising, meaning the rescue. Only raising is discussed, because lowering someone into a pit is not a favor anyone pays for.

keyTerms.meaning: That which was taught in a ברייתא
Shepherds of small animals (sheep and goats)

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר רַב יוֹסֵף לְמֵימַר, הָא דְּתַנְיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef thought to say, about what was taught:
Gentiles and shepherds of small animals,
we do not raise them up and do not lower them down;
phrases.notes: This is talking about a pit: we don't pull them out, and we don't push them in.

phrases.english: raising them for pay is permitted, because of hostility.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר רַב יוֹסֵף לְמֵימַר, הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the איבה reasoning to a third case, taken from a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggested: pulling a non-Jew out of a pit for pay is allowed because of איבה.

steps.title: אביי: he can say he is busy
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the idea. The Jew can say his son is up on the roof, or that he has a court appointment, so refusing causes no hostility.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: he can tell him, 'My son is standing on the roof,' or, 'I have an appointment at the court.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his third and final rejection. Here too the Jew has an easy excuse, so there is no איבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These excuses make the refusal look like a scheduling problem, not hatred. As in the first two cases, once a believable excuse exists, the fear of איבה is gone, and the ברייתא's איסור stands even when payment is offered.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף tried three times to use איבה to permit something forbidden: delivering on שבת, nursing, and raising from a pit. אביי answered the same way each time. איבה only applies when there is no believable excuse for refusing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a clear limit on איבה. It permits an act only when a refusal cannot be explained in a non-hostile way.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
He can say to him:
"My son is standing on the roof,"
phrases.notes: He is saying he needs his ladder or rope for his son right now, so he can't use it for the pit.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי ״נְקִיטָא לִי זִימְנָא לְבֵי דַוָּאר״.
phrases.english: or else, "I have an appointment at the courthouse."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: יָכוֹל לוֹמַר לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's suggestion in step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects permitting a paid rescue from the pit because of איבה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Jew can give a believable excuse, so no איבה results.

steps.title: רבי אבהו recites a teaching before רבי יוחנן about not raising certain people
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו recites a ברייתא in front of רבי יוחנן: גוים and shepherds of small animals are not raised up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו taught in front of רבי יוחנן: גוים and shepherds of small animals, we do not raise them up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching, recited by רבי אבהו before his teacher רבי יוחנן, that starts with the rule of not raising גוים and small-animal shepherds. This line opens the teaching, and the rest of it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sounds like the ברייתא that רב יוסף quoted in Step 22, but now it comes through a different chain: רבי אבהו in front of רבי יוחנן. The גמרא is starting this version again because רבי אבהו's teaching goes on to add more cases. Right now, only the opening rule appears: we do not raise them up.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of; in the presence of (a teacher)
Shepherds of small animals, like sheep and goats
We do not raise them up (out of a pit)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not just a copy of Step 22. The same opening words come back because רבי אבהו's version is a separate teaching that will continue with more cases.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu taught before Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Gentiles and shepherds of small animals
— one does not raise them up
phrases.notes: He means pulling them up out of a pit, like the case in the earlier ברייתא from Step 22.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth between רב יוסף and אביי ends, the גמרא brings a related teaching from רבי אבהו about raising people from a pit. This teaching is the start of a longer statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גוים and shepherds of small animals are not raised up (out of a pit).
